'''Barbara Imperiali''' (born 1 January 1957) is a Professor of Biology and Chemistry at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] and Affiliate Member of the [[Broad Institute]]. She is an elected member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] and a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]].

== Education and early career ==
Barbara Imperiali was raised in England and attended the Southbank School in [[Caterham]] in [[Surrey]], followed by Coloma Grammar School in [[Croydon]] where she specialized in studying the sciences.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Viegas|first=J.|date=2013-12-02|title=Profile of Barbara Imperiali|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=110|issue=52|pages=20850–20851|doi=10.1073/pnas.1321020110|pmid=24297879|pmc=3876202|bibcode=2013PNAS..11020850V|issn=0027-8424|doi-access=free}}</ref> She received her [[Bachelor of Science]] in [[Medicinal Chemistry]] from the [[University College London]] in 1979. She attended [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], where she received her [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in [[synthetic organic chemistry]] in 1983. She joined the lab of Satoru Masamune, working to develop and apply new techniques to synthesize a class of [[Antibiotics|antibiotic]] chemicals known as [[ansamycin]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Masamune|first1=Satoru|last2=Imperiali|first2=Barbara|last3=Garvey|first3=David S.|date=1982-10-01|title=Synthesis of ansamycins: the ansa chain of rifamycin S|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=104|issue=20|pages=5528–5531|doi=10.1021/ja00384a063|bibcode=1982JAChS.104.5528M |issn=0002-7863}}</ref> As a postdoc in the Masamune lab she worked with the enzyme [[HADHB|beta-ketothiolase]].<ref name=":0" />

She did additional postdoctoral research at [[Brandeis University]] in the laboratory of Robert Abeles, where she received training in [[chemical biology]] designing, synthesizing, and evaluating peptide-based [[protease inhibitors]].<ref name=":0" />

== Research ==
In 1986, Imperiali became an assistant professor at [[Carnegie Mellon University]] before moving her laboratory to [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1989. While at Caltech, she was influenced by the research of [[Dennis A. Dougherty|Dennis Dougherty]], who was applying unnatural amino acid mutagenesis to understand interactions of ligand-gated membrane channels and receptors. Imperiali's work became focused on problems at the chemistry–biology interface, using chemistry to better understand the structure and function of proteins ''in vivo''.<ref name=":0" />

In 1999, she returned to MIT as the [[Ellen Swallow Richards]] Professor of Biology.<ref name=":0" /> Her research program is focused on  protein [[glycosylation]], a process by which a carbohydrate is added to a protein to change its structure or function. Her lab has developed techniques to track and understand how glycosylation at the time of protein production—a process known as [[Translation (biology)|translation]]—affects protein folding and conformation. Applying techniques such as [[Fluorescence Resonance Energy Transfer]] and [[nuclear magnetic resonance]], she has elucidated how glycosylation might protect proteins against misfolding and how it affects folding mechanics and thermodynamic stability.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bosques|first1=Carlos J.|last2=Imperiali|first2=Barbara|date=2003-06-24|title=The interplay of glycosylation and disulfide formation influences fibrillization in a prion protein fragment|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=100|issue=13|pages=7593–7598|doi=10.1073/pnas.1232504100|issn=0027-8424|pmid=12805563|pmc=164631|bibcode=2003PNAS..100.7593B|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=Mark M.|last2=Bartlett|first2=Alice I.|last3=Nerenberg|first3=Paul S.|last4=Friel|first4=Claire T.|last5=Hackenberger|first5=Christian P. R.|last6=Stultz|first6=Collin M.|last7=Radford|first7=Sheena E.|last8=Imperiali|first8=Barbara|date=2010-12-28|title=Perturbing the folding energy landscape of the bacterial immunity protein Im7 by site-specific N-linked glycosylation|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=107|issue=52|pages=22528–22533|doi=10.1073/pnas.1015356107|issn=0027-8424|pmid=21148421|pmc=3012502|bibcode=2010PNAS..10722528C|doi-access=free}}</ref>

In addition to studying glycosylation, Imperiali has also led investigations into how to design, develop, and apply chemical approaches to understand and manipulate biochemical processes for a variety of applications. Her group has collaborated to develop a fluorescence-based method to detect [[phosphorylation]] of [[peptide]]s and [[protein]]s to monitor the activity of [[kinases]], which are enzymes that catalyze phosphorylation and coordinate a vast array of cellular activities.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shults|first1=Melissa D.|last2=Janes|first2=Kevin A.|last3=Lauffenburger|first3=Douglas A.|last4=Imperiali|first4=Barbara|date=April 2005|title=A multiplexed homogeneous fluorescence-based assay for protein kinase activity in cell lysates|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nmeth747|journal=Nature Methods|language=en|volume=2|issue=4|pages=277–284|doi=10.1038/nmeth747|pmid=15782220|s2cid=23797954|issn=1548-7105|url-access=subscription}}</ref> This method can be applied to screen for [[protein kinase inhibitor]]s and monitor their activities in cells and tissues, enabling tracking of signaling pathways and providing a potential diagnostic tool for diseases like cancers that may result from disrupted kinase-mediated regulation.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Stains|first1=Cliff I.|last2=Tedford|first2=Nathan C.|last3=Walkup|first3=Traci C.|last4=Luković|first4=Elvedin|last5=Goguen|first5=Brenda N.|last6=Griffith|first6=Linda G.|last7=Lauffenburger|first7=Douglas A.|last8=Imperiali|first8=Barbara|date=2012-02-24|title=Interrogating Signaling Nodes Involved in Cellular Transformations Using Kinase Activity Probes|journal=Chemistry & Biology|language=en|volume=19|issue=2|pages=210–217|doi=10.1016/j.chembiol.2011.11.012|pmid=22365604|pmc=3307342|issn=1074-5521|doi-access=free}}</ref>

She has also authored the textbook ''Chemical Glycobiology''.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Imperiali|first=Barbara|url=http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/bookseries/00766879/597|title=Chemical Glycobiology. Part A, Part A|date=2017|publisher=Academic Press |isbn=978-0-12-811470-4|oclc=1004589170}}</ref>
